event.canonical_title: South Carolina Holds Special Election for Lindsey Graham's Senate Seat
event.summary: Republican voters in South Carolina are participating in a special election to select a candidate to replace the late Senator Lindsey Graham. This election marks the second time in two months that voters are heading to the polls for this seat, which has gained attention due to the circumstances surrounding Graham's death.

event_overview.title: About South Carolina Senate
event_overview.subject: South Carolina Senate
event_overview.summary: This is a statewide South Carolina Republican special primary process to replace the party’s U.S. Senate nominee after that nominee died, not a special election to fill a vacant U.S. Senate office. The resulting Republican nominee is scheduled to appear on the November 3, 2026, general-election ballot for U.S. Senate.

facts.label: Purpose and legal basis
facts.value: The South Carolina State Election Commission said the process was triggered by the death of the Republican Party’s U.S. Senate nominee and is being conducted under S.C. Code § 7-11-55.

facts.label: Jurisdiction and administrator
facts.value: It is a statewide Republican primary administered by the South Carolina State Election Commission.

facts.label: Election schedule
facts.value: The special primary was held August 11, 2026; the Election Commission scheduled a runoff, if necessary, for August 25, 2026, with early voting August 19-21.

facts.label: Participation rules
facts.value: Voters who participated in South Carolina’s June Democratic primary were ineligible for this Republican special primary; voters who participated in the June Republican primary or did not vote in either June primary were eligible.

facts.label: How the nominee is selected
facts.value: Under § 7-11-55, a party-nominee vacancy following death, disqualification, or an approved legitimate nonpolitical resignation is filled through a special primary; the statute provides for a runoff when necessary and requires timely certification for the general election.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the August 2026 special Republican nomination contest and any runoff developments, not the full November general-election campaign or a separate vacancy process for an occupied Senate seat.
